Watching the slightly choppy sea from a boat, the last thing I felt like doing was embarking on another 5km (3-mile) swim. Mind fog had sapped my energy, and my mood was decidedly Eeyore-like. item.title: Tibetan river hosting world’s biggest dam is facing increasing flood risk: study
item.description: Chinese researchers have found that the Yarlung Tsangpo River – soon to host the largest mega dam in the world – may face increased run-off and flood risks over this century. Using tree-ring width chronologies in the southeastern Tibetan Plateau, the team reconstructed the river’s run-off history from 1325 to 2020. Along with climate data, this was used to create a model that projected river run-off would increase under future climate scenarios, along with a possible increase in high-run-off... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.description: More inclement weather forecast in rain-soaked Four Corners region after evacuations and rescues last week Another round of heavy showers and thunderstorms were expected to hit the south-west US on Sunday after the region endured days of rain that forced evacuations, water rescues and multi-million-dollar damage. The National Weather Service issued a flood watch for much of the Four Corners – the meeting point of Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico and Utah – even as local officials forecast further receding of swollen rivers that surged since rains picked up on Wednesday. item.title: The Guardian view on Oxford Street’s pedestrianisation: cities should be designed around people, not cars | Editorial
item.description: The transformation of Europe’s busiest shopping street should be a case study in making cities greener, less congested and more inviting places to live Sadiq Khan has been trying to pedestrianise Oxford Street since he first became the mayor of London in 2016. On Monday, after numerous setbacks, his plan will finally come to fruition. The busiest stretch of the nation’s famous shopping street will be closed to traffic in a scheme designed to improve the area and make it more attractive to pedestrians. It should be an emblematic case study in making cities greener, less congested, more… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: Las abejas europeas han perdido un tercio de su territorio en un siglo. Y el cambio climático no es el principal culpable
item.description: Desde pequeños nos enseñan que las abejas son fundamentales para la supervivencia de la humanidad gracias a su capacidad de polinización. El problema llega cuando los datos de los que disponemos nos informan que las abejas europeas han perdido aproximadamente un tercio de su territorio en los últimos cien años. Y no se trata de una estimación al aire, sino de la conclusión a la que ha llegado la Estación Biológica de Doñana, que ha logrado mapear el declive de nuestros polinizadores. Viene de lejos. Para saber hacia dónde vamos, primero hay que saber de dónde venimos. Ese ha sido el objetivo… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: Arctic ice had been expanding for 1,000 years before reaching its greatest extent around 1960
item.description: A recent study indicates that the Barnes Ice Cap had begun expanding nearly 2,000 years ago. This expansion was attributed to cooler summer conditions that allowed ice to grow. However, rising greenhouse gas emissions reversed this trend and caused significant ice retreat since the 1960s. Researchers emphasize that human-induced warming has disrupted natural climate patterns that favored renewed glacial growth. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Microorganisms show promise for reducing emissions from manure
item.description: Dairy farmers sometimes use additives in their cattle housing to reduce emissions from slurry. Emissions of substances such as ammonia occur when urine and feces mix on the floor of the housing. At the same time, dairy farmers want to increase the fertilizing value of the manure when it is applied to agricultural land. Fuente: Phys.org.
